brief:
Middle East Eye examines how residents of Gaza have adapted to life under sustained conflict, describing how extreme conditions have become embedded in patterns of daily existence. The outlet characterizes these survival routines as ritualized, suggesting that horror has become normalized through constant repetition and familiarity across months of crisis.

The report emphasizes how scenes of devastation have become commonplace across screens and in lived experience, with viewers and residents alike developing a kind of habituation to acute hardship. According to the outlet, the cumulative weight of these recurring traumas has fundamentally altered the texture of civilian life in the territory, reshaping what residents consider ordinary.
dek: Gaza genocide: How Israel made horror a ritual of daily life Life under genocide has its familiar daily rituals. A discerning eye detects latent horrors in the scenes that unfold in succession across screens. Elsewhere, the scene itself disappears beneath…
title: Gaza civilians navigate daily survival amid ongoing conflict, Middle East Eye reports
